**It's not recipe data at all.** Compare the two:
- Run 1 (response_format on): `name='Chicken Biryani' ingredients=[...] time_minutes=90` — actual recipe, validated Pydantic object.
- Run 2 (response_format off): `{"name": "Recipe", "schema": {...}}` — this has keys `name` and `schema`. Not `ingredients`, not `time_minutes`. If you ran `Recipe.model_validate_json()` on it, it'd throw `ValidationError` immediately — missing required fields.

**Why the model produced that shape:** look at [app.py:15](week02-structured-output/app.py#L15):
```python
system_prompt = "...respond only with JSON matching this schema: {'name': 'Recipe', 'schema': Recipe.model_json_schema()}"
```
That's a plain string, not an f-string. `Recipe.model_json_schema()` never executes — the model literally receives the raw characters `{'name': 'Recipe', 'schema': Recipe.model_json_schema()}` as text. So instead of seeing an actual JSON Schema to follow, the model sees a confusing snippet shaped like `{"name": ..., "schema": ...}` and — without `response_format` constraining it — did the most literal-minded thing: it produced JSON matching *that* shape (mimicking a generic JSON-Schema-looking object) instead of your real Recipe fields. It also wrapped the whole thing in ```` ```json ```` fences, which would break `json.loads` too.

So what looks "cleaner" (typed properties, descriptions, `required` arrays) is the model pattern-matching on "JSON Schema" as a concept and hallucinating a plausible-looking one — not obeying your actual Recipe model. It's confidently wrong, which is worse than obviously wrong.

**This is exactly the point of the ablation you ran.** Without `response_format`:
- prompt-text bugs (like the missing `f`) directly corrupt output
- no shape guarantee at all, model free-associates on confusing instructions

- Groq's constrained decoding ignores the prompt confusion and forces valid Recipe-shaped tokens regardless
- that's why run 1 worked even though the same buggy prompt text was present

system_prompt = "You are a chef with 25+ years of experience. ... respond only with JSON."

# AI Career Roadmap — Project Context

Full plan: [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md). This file is the working-session summary.

## Who's working here

22yo, BTech CSE, ~6mo Junior SWE (AI/ML), Hyderabad, ₹6 LPA. Knows Python, FastAPI (not pro), Docker, some React/Java, RAG/LLM/LangChain basics.

Redoing Phase 1 on purpose — not first exposure. Goal: verify fundamentals, catch gaps, actually ship the 3 projects. Don't over-explain things already known; probe first.

## Current status

**Phase 1 — Foundation (mo 1-3, wk 1-12).** Starting at Week 1.

Update this line as weeks/checkpoints complete: `Currently: Week X — <topic>`.

## Phase 1 target (12 weeks)

3 public, deployed, evaluated projects:
1. LLM tool, structured output + tool calling (wk 1-3)
2. RAG system w/ citations, deployed (wk 4-6)
3. Tool-using agent w/ eval harness (wk 7-9)

Wk 10-12: cost/latency optimization + polish + writeups across all three.

Learning:building ratio ~40:60 this phase — lean toward building.

## Week-by-week (Phase 1)

| Wk | Learn | Build |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | System/user prompts, few-shot, hosted model API | CLI script: prompt → raw text |
| 2 | Forced JSON output, Pydantic validation, retry-on-invalid | Typed/validated JSON output |
| 3 | Tool/function calling schemas | Finish tool, README, public repo |
| 4 | Embeddings, chunking strategies | Chunk a real corpus |
| 5 | Vector DB, similarity + hybrid search | Index corpus, basic retrieval |
| 6 | Context assembly, citations | Full RAG + deploy (Render/Railway/Fly.io) — **Checkpoint 1** |
| 7 | Agent loops, ReAct, LangGraph | Minimal agent, 1 real tool |
| 8 | Multi-tool orchestration, memory/state | Agent w/ 2-3 tools, multi-step task |
| 9 | Evals for non-deterministic systems, RAGAS/LangSmith | Eval harness + guardrails |
| 10 | Token cost math, latency sources, caching | Instrument cost/latency tracking |
| 11 | Model routing, prompt caching, batching | Implement 1-2 optimizations, measure |
| 12 | — | Polish all 3, public writeups — **Checkpoint 1 major** |

### Checkpoint 1 (major, end of month 3) — pass criteria
- [ ] 3 projects public + deployed (not just repos)
- [ ] Each has an eval or measured before/after
- [ ] Can explain every architectural choice under questioning
- [ ] One honest written failure case per project

Short on 1-2 → spend an extra week here before Phase 2. This gate matters more than the calendar.

## After Phase 1

- **Phase 2** (mo 4-6): DSA (NeetCode150/Blind75) + system design basics + pick specialization (leaning Context Engineering / Agentic AI Engineering; LLMOps backup)
- **Phase 3** (mo 7-12): specialization depth, project #2, visibility, resume v1
- **Phase 4** (mo 13-18): market readiness, mock interviews
- **Phase 5** (mo 19-24+): apply in batches, track outcomes

Full detail for these phases lives in [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md) — only Phase 1/2 are planned week-by-week on purpose.

## Resources (Phase 1)

- Anthropic Messages API docs, OpenAI API docs
- DeepLearning.AI short courses (free) — prompt engineering, RAG, agentic RAG
- Pydantic docs
- LangChain / LangGraph docs
- pgvector / Chroma / Qdrant
- RAGAS, LangSmith
- Render / Railway / Fly.io (deploy)

## Working rules for this repo

- Don't skip checkpoints — they're the anti-rabbit-hole mechanism.
- Every deliverable ships public (repo/demo/writeup), not left private.
- When user drifts off current week's scope, redirect back to it.
- User's global CLAUDE.md still applies (junior-dev teaching mode, explain WHY, flag "💡 Learn this" concepts, tests alongside code, no debug prints, direct communication).

## Standards

- Follow **PEP 8** conventions
- Use **type annotations** on all function signatures

## Immutability

Prefer immutable data structures:

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class User:
    name: str
    email: str

from typing import NamedTuple

class Point(NamedTuple):
    x: float
    y: float
```

## Formatting

- **black** for code formatting
- **isort** for import sorting
- **ruff** for linting

See skill: `python-patterns` for comprehensive Python idioms and patterns.

content.text:
4 bugs stacked here, not 1:

**1. api_key never loads — root cause of error you see**
[app.py:6](week01-prompting/app.py#L6) reads `os.getenv("GROQ_API_KEY")` but nowhere in app.py calls `load_dotenv()`. Your [config.py](week01-prompting/config.py) does call it — but app.py never imports config.py, so that code never runs. `os.getenv` only sees real OS env vars, not `.env` file contents, unless something loads the file first.

**2. `.env` doesn't even exist**
Checked — week01-prompting/ has no `.env` file at all. Fix #1 alone won't help; getenv returns None regardless.

**3. Groq key + openai client, no base_url override**
`openai.api_key = ...` sets auth, but openai SDK still points at `api.openai.com` by default. Groq's key won't authenticate there — you'd hit a 401 next, not this error. Groq exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1`; SDK needs `base_url` set to that (or use `groq` package's own client instead).

**4. Wrong endpoint for the model**
`openai.completions.create` is legacy text-completion API (raw `prompt` string). `gpt-oss-120b` is a chat model — needs `chat.completions.create` with `messages=[{"role": "system", ...}, {"role": "user", ...}]`, not `prompt=`.

💡 Learn this: `.env` files are inert text until something calls `load_dotenv()` **before** the code that reads `os.getenv()` runs — import order matters. And "api_key set" ≠ "pointed at right server" — SDK base_url and provider are separate concerns.

Per your ask — go fix these 4 yourself, I'll review after. Also logging this pattern in CLAUDE.md now.

# AI Career Roadmap — Project Context

Full plan: [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md). This file is the working-session summary.

## Who's working here

22yo, BTech CSE, ~6mo Junior SWE (AI/ML), Hyderabad, ₹6 LPA. Knows Python, FastAPI (not pro), Docker, some React/Java, RAG/LLM/LangChain basics.

Redoing Phase 1 on purpose — not first exposure. Goal: verify fundamentals, catch gaps, actually ship the 3 projects. Don't over-explain things already known; probe first.

## Current status

**Phase 1 — Foundation (mo 1-3, wk 1-12).** Starting at Week 1.

Update this line as weeks/checkpoints complete: `Currently: Week X — <topic>`.

## Phase 1 target (12 weeks)

3 public, deployed, evaluated projects:
1. LLM tool, structured output + tool calling (wk 1-3)
2. RAG system w/ citations, deployed (wk 4-6)
3. Tool-using agent w/ eval harness (wk 7-9)

Wk 10-12: cost/latency optimization + polish + writeups across all three.

Learning:building ratio ~40:60 this phase — lean toward building.

## Week-by-week (Phase 1)

| Wk | Learn | Build |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | System/user prompts, few-shot, hosted model API | CLI script: prompt → raw text |
| 2 | Forced JSON output, Pydantic validation, retry-on-invalid | Typed/validated JSON output |
| 3 | Tool/function calling schemas | Finish tool, README, public repo |
| 4 | Embeddings, chunking strategies | Chunk a real corpus |
| 5 | Vector DB, similarity + hybrid search | Index corpus, basic retrieval |
| 6 | Context assembly, citations | Full RAG + deploy (Render/Railway/Fly.io) — **Checkpoint 1** |
| 7 | Agent loops, ReAct, LangGraph | Minimal agent, 1 real tool |
| 8 | Multi-tool orchestration, memory/state | Agent w/ 2-3 tools, multi-step task |
| 9 | Evals for non-deterministic systems, RAGAS/LangSmith | Eval harness + guardrails |
| 10 | Token cost math, latency sources, caching | Instrument cost/latency tracking |
| 11 | Model routing, prompt caching, batching | Implement 1-2 optimizations, measure |
| 12 | — | Polish all 3, public writeups — **Checkpoint 1 major** |

### Checkpoint 1 (major, end of month 3) — pass criteria
- [ ] 3 projects public + deployed (not just repos)
- [ ] Each has an eval or measured before/after
- [ ] Can explain every architectural choice under questioning
- [ ] One honest written failure case per project

Short on 1-2 → spend an extra week here before Phase 2. This gate matters more than the calendar.

## After Phase 1

- **Phase 2** (mo 4-6): DSA (NeetCode150/Blind75) + system design basics + pick specialization (leaning Context Engineering / Agentic AI Engineering; LLMOps backup)
- **Phase 3** (mo 7-12): specialization depth, project #2, visibility, resume v1
- **Phase 4** (mo 13-18): market readiness, mock interviews
- **Phase 5** (mo 19-24+): apply in batches, track outcomes

Full detail for these phases lives in [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md) — only Phase 1/2 are planned week-by-week on purpose.

## Resources (Phase 1)

- Anthropic Messages API docs, OpenAI API docs
- DeepLearning.AI short courses (free) — prompt engineering, RAG, agentic RAG
- Pydantic docs
- LangChain / LangGraph docs
- pgvector / Chroma / Qdrant
- RAGAS, LangSmith
- Render / Railway / Fly.io (deploy)

## Working rules for this repo

- Don't skip checkpoints — they're the anti-rabbit-hole mechanism.
- Every deliverable ships public (repo/demo/writeup), not left private.
- When user drifts off current week's scope, redirect back to it.
- User's global CLAUDE.md still applies (junior-dev teaching mode, explain WHY, flag "💡 Learn this" concepts, tests alongside code, no debug prints, direct communication).

# a CLI script that sends a prompt(system + user) and returns raw text.

import os
import openai
from config import groq_api_key

system_prompt = "You are a helpful assistant that answers questions based on the provided context. Be to the point and give concise answers. If you don't know the answer, say 'I don't know'. Do not make up answers. Give straight answers, no sentence fragments."
user_prompt = "What is the capital of France? And what is the population of France?"

prompt = system_prompt + "\n" + user_prompt

client = openai.OpenAI(
    api_key=groq_api_key,
    base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1",
)

completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-oss-20b", #openai/gpt-oss-20b, openai/gpt-oss-120b
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    max_tokens=200,
    temperature=0.5,
)

print(completion.choices[0].message.content)

content.text:
Script logic all correct — this is a new, unrelated bug: Windows console encoding.

**Root cause:** PowerShell's default console codepage (cp1252 / Windows-1252) can't represent every Unicode character. Model returned a narrow no-break space (`U+202F`, common in numbers like "68 000 000" formatting) — cp1252 has no mapping for it, so `print()` crashes trying to encode it for the terminal.

Not a Groq/API bug — it's a Windows-terminal-vs-Python-vs-Unicode mismatch you'll hit again anytime a model returns non-ASCII (curly quotes, em-dashes, foreign chars, etc.).

💡 Learn this: Python's `print()` encodes using the console's codepage, not UTF-8, by default on Windows. Two common fixes:
1. Force stdout to UTF-8 in the script (`sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")` near the top).
2. Or switch terminal codepage: `chcp 65001` before running, or set `$env:PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8"`.

Pick one, apply it, rerun — ping me with output.

Yes, exactly right. Two camps, not "every vendor totally different":

**Camp 1 — OpenAI-compatible** (what you just used)
Groq, Together, OpenRouter, Fireworks, Deepseek, local Ollama/LM Studio — all mimic OpenAI's `chat.completions` shape. Swap `base_url` + `api_key`, same `messages=[...]`, same `client.chat.completions.create()`, same `response.choices[0].message.content`. This is why your Groq code looks identical to real OpenAI code — intentional, OpenAI's shape became the de facto standard.

**Camp 2 — native SDKs, real divergence**
- **Anthropic**: `system` is a separate top-level param, not a `"system"` role in the messages list. Response is `response.content[0].text`, not `.choices[0].message.content`. Content is a list of blocks (text/tool_use/image), not a flat string.
- **Gemini**: `contents=[...]` not `messages=[...]`, roles are `user`/`model` not `user`/`assistant`, safety_settings param, different SDK (`google-genai`).
- Each has own auth header convention, own streaming event format, own tool/function-calling JSON schema (though these are converging toward OpenAI's shape too, since it's become quasi-standard even Anthropic/Google mostly follow now).

**What's experience vs. learn-now:**

Experience = memorizing exact field names per vendor. Don't grind that.

Learn now (transferable, applies to any new SDK you meet):
1. Fixed 4-step mental checklist you just lived through — (a) load key safely, (b) find right client/base_url, (c) match request schema to their docs, (d) parse their response shape. Every new provider = same 4 steps, different values.
2. Reading API docs cold and mapping auth → request → response, rather than copy-pasting examples blind.
3. Abstraction libraries exist for exactly this pain — LiteLLM, LangChain's chat model classes — normalize all providers into one interface. Worth knowing they exist; don't reach for them yet, raw SDK first builds the intuition those libraries paper over.

Function/tool calling schema differences — that's literally your Week 3 topic, comes next, don't rabbit hole into it now.

Two camps, not "every vendor totally different":

**Camp 1 — OpenAI-compatible** (what you just used)
Groq, Together, OpenRouter, Fireworks, Deepseek, local Ollama/LM Studio — all mimic OpenAI's `chat.completions` shape. Swap `base_url` + `api_key`, same `messages=[...]`, same `client.chat.completions.create()`, same `response.choices[0].message.content`. This is why your Groq code looks identical to real OpenAI code — intentional, OpenAI's shape became the de facto standard.

**Camp 2 — native SDKs, real divergence**
- **Anthropic**: `system` is a separate top-level param, not a `"system"` role in the messages list. Response is `response.content[0].text`, not `.choices[0].message.content`. Content is a list of blocks (text/tool_use/image), not a flat string.
- **Gemini**: `contents=[...]` not `messages=[...]`, roles are `user`/`model` not `user`/`assistant`, safety_settings param, different SDK (`google-genai`).
- Each has own auth header convention, own streaming event format, own tool/function-calling JSON schema (though these are converging toward OpenAI's shape too, since it's become quasi-standard even Anthropic/Google mostly follow now).

**What's experience vs. learn-now:**

Experience = memorizing exact field names per vendor. Don't grind that.

Learn now (transferable, applies to any new SDK you meet):
1. Fixed 4-step mental checklist you just lived through — (a) load key safely, (b) find right client/base_url, (c) match request schema to their docs, (d) parse their response shape. Every new provider = same 4 steps, different values.
2. Reading API docs cold and mapping auth → request → response, rather than copy-pasting examples blind.
3. Abstraction libraries exist for exactly this pain — LiteLLM, LangChain's chat model classes — normalize all providers into one interface. Worth knowing they exist; don't reach for them yet, raw SDK first builds the intuition those libraries paper over.

Function/tool calling schema differences — that's literally your Week 3 topic, comes next, don't rabbit hole into it now.","background_tasks":[],"session_crons":[]}

Watch for repeats when adding new scripts/modules that need secrets.
94	- **SDK client vs. provider endpoint mismatch** (2026-08-05, Wk1 app.py): set `openai.api_key` to a Groq key, but never overrode `base_url` — SDK still points at OpenAI's servers by default. 1	# AI Career Roadmap — Project Context
2	
3	Full plan: [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md). This file is the working-session summary.
4	
5	## Who's working here
6	
7	22yo, BTech CSE, ~6mo Junior SWE (AI/ML), Hyderabad, ₹6 LPA. Knows Python, FastAPI (not pro), Docker, some React/Java, RAG/LLM/LangChain basics.
8	
9	Redoing Phase 1 on purpose — not first exposure. Goal: verify fundamentals, catch gaps, actually ship the 3 projects. Don't over-explain things already known; probe first.
10	
11	## Current status
12	
13	**Phase 1 — Foundation (mo 1-3, wk 1-12).** Starting at Week 1.
14	
15	Update this line as weeks/checkpoints complete: `Currently: Week X — <topic>`.
16	
17	## Phase 1 target (12 weeks)
18	
19	3 public, deployed, evaluated projects:
20	1. LLM tool, structured output + tool calling (wk 1-3)
21	2. RAG system w/ citations, deployed (wk 4-6)
22	3. Tool-using agent w/ eval harness (wk 7-9)
23	
24	Wk 10-12: cost/latency optimization + polish + writeups across all three.
25	
26	Learning:building ratio ~40:60 this phase — lean toward building.
27	
28	## Week-by-week (Phase 1)
29	
30	| Wk | Learn | Build |
31	|---|---|---|
32	| 1 | System/user prompts, few-shot, hosted model API | CLI script: prompt → raw text |
33	| 2 | Forced JSON output, Pydantic validation, retry-on-invalid | Typed/validated JSON output |
34	| 3 | Tool/function calling schemas | Finish tool, README, public repo |
35	| 4 | Embeddings, chunking strategies | Chunk a real corpus |
36	| 5 | Vector DB, similarity + hybrid search | Index corpus, basic retrieval |
37	| 6 | Context assembly, citations | Full RAG + deploy (Render/Railway/Fly.io) — **Checkpoint 1** |
38	| 7 | Agent loops, ReAct, LangGraph | Minimal agent, 1 real tool |
39	| 8 | Multi-tool orchestration, memory/state | Agent w/ 2-3 tools, multi-step task |
40	| 9 | Evals for non-deterministic systems, RAGAS/LangSmith | Eval harness + guardrails |
41	| 10 | Token cost math, latency sources, caching | Instrument cost/latency tracking |
42	| 11 | Model routing, prompt caching, batching | Implement 1-2 optimizations, measure |
43	| 12 | — | Polish all 3, public writeups — **Checkpoint 1 major** |
44	
45	### Checkpoint 1 (major, end of month 3) — pass criteria
46	- [ ] 3 projects public + deployed (not just repos)
47	- [ ] Each has an eval or measured before/after
48	- [ ] Can explain every architectural choice under questioning
49	- [ ] One honest written failure case per project
50	
51	Short on 1-2 → spend an extra week here before Phase 2. This gate matters more than the calendar.
52	
53	## After Phase 1
54	
55	- **Phase 2** (mo 4-6): DSA (NeetCode150/Blind75) + system design basics + pick specialization (leaning Context Engineering / Agentic AI Engineering; LLMOps backup)
56	- **Phase 3** (mo 7-12): specialization depth, project #2, visibility, resume v1
57	- **Phase 4** (mo 13-18): market readiness, mock interviews

# AI Career Roadmap — Project Context

Full plan: [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md). This file is the working-session summary.

## Who's working here

22yo, BTech CSE, ~6mo Junior SWE (AI/ML), Hyderabad, ₹6 LPA. Knows Python, FastAPI (not pro), Docker, some React/Java, RAG/LLM/LangChain basics.

Redoing Phase 1 on purpose — not first exposure. Goal: verify fundamentals, catch gaps, actually ship the 3 projects. Don't over-explain things already known; probe first.

## Current status

**Phase 1 — Foundation (mo 1-3, wk 1-12).** Starting at Week 1.

Update this line as weeks/checkpoints complete: `Currently: Week X — <topic>`.

## Phase 1 target (12 weeks)

3 public, deployed, evaluated projects:
1. LLM tool, structured output + tool calling (wk 1-3)
2. RAG system w/ citations, deployed (wk 4-6)
3. Tool-using agent w/ eval harness (wk 7-9)

Wk 10-12: cost/latency optimization + polish + writeups across all three.

Learning:building ratio ~40:60 this phase — lean toward building.

## Week-by-week (Phase 1)

| Wk | Learn | Build |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | System/user prompts, few-shot, hosted model API | CLI script: prompt → raw text |
| 2 | Forced JSON output, Pydantic validation, retry-on-invalid | Typed/validated JSON output |
| 3 | Tool/function calling schemas | Finish tool, README, public repo |
| 4 | Embeddings, chunking strategies | Chunk a real corpus |
| 5 | Vector DB, similarity + hybrid search | Index corpus, basic retrieval |
| 6 | Context assembly, citations | Full RAG + deploy (Render/Railway/Fly.io) — **Checkpoint 1** |
| 7 | Agent loops, ReAct, LangGraph | Minimal agent, 1 real tool |
| 8 | Multi-tool orchestration, memory/state | Agent w/ 2-3 tools, multi-step task |
| 9 | Evals for non-deterministic systems, RAGAS/LangSmith | Eval harness + guardrails |
| 10 | Token cost math, latency sources, caching | Instrument cost/latency tracking |
| 11 | Model routing, prompt caching, batching | Implement 1-2 optimizations, measure |
| 12 | — | Polish all 3, public writeups — **Checkpoint 1 major** |

### Checkpoint 1 (major, end of month 3) — pass criteria
- [ ] 3 projects public + deployed (not just repos)
- [ ] Each has an eval or measured before/after
- [ ] Can explain every architectural choice under questioning
- [ ] One honest written failure case per project

Short on 1-2 → spend an extra week here before Phase 2. This gate matters more than the calendar.

## After Phase 1

- **Phase 2** (mo 4-6): DSA (NeetCode150/Blind75) + system design basics + pick specialization (leaning Context Engineering / Agentic AI Engineering; LLMOps backup)
- **Phase 3** (mo 7-12): specialization depth, project #2, visibility, resume v1
- **Phase 4** (mo 13-18): market readiness, mock interviews
- **Phase 5** (mo 19-24+): apply in batches, track outcomes

Full detail for these phases lives in [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md) — only Phase 1/2 are planned week-by-week on purpose.

## Resources (Phase 1)

- Anthropic Messages API docs, OpenAI API docs
- DeepLearning.AI short courses (free) — prompt engineering, RAG, agentic RAG
- Pydantic docs
- LangChain / LangGraph docs
- pgvector / Chroma / Qdrant
- RAGAS, LangSmith
- Render / Railway / Fly.io (deploy)

## Working rules for this repo

- Don't skip checkpoints — they're the anti-rabbit-hole mechanism.
- Every deliverable ships public (repo/demo/writeup), not left private.
- When user drifts off current week's scope, redirect back to it.
- User's global CLAUDE.md still applies (junior-dev teaching mode, explain WHY, flag "💡 Learn this" concepts, tests alongside code, no debug prints, direct communication).

## Architecture diagrams (Excalidraw)

Maintain a living system-design/architecture diagram per project via the Excalidraw MCP server (already configured — `mcp__excalidraw__*` tools). Update it incrementally, don't regenerate from scratch, every time new code or a structural change lands during that week's session.

- One diagram per project: wk1-3 tool, wk4-6 RAG system, wk7-9 agent (3 total across Phase 1)
- Update after each build session, not just at project end — diagram tracks current code, not the final design
- Use `create_element` / `batch_create_elements` for new components, `update_element` for changed ones, `delete_element` for removed ones. Never `clear_canvas` + redraw — that loses history
- Show real system boundaries: scripts/modules, API calls (incl. which provider/endpoint), data stores, external services, request/response flow — not abstract concepts
- When a snapshot is needed for a project writeup, use `export_scene` or `get_canvas_screenshot`

## Recurring small-detail gaps (watch + reinforce)

Track patterns here when Ved hits the same *kind* of bug more than once, so foundations actually solidify instead of getting patched over each time.

- **Env var loading order** (2026-08-05, Wk1 app.py): wrote `os.getenv()` in a file that never called `load_dotenv()` — had it in a separate `config.py` that was never imported. `.env` is inert until something loads it *before* the read happens; import order matters. Watch for repeats when adding new scripts/modules that need secrets.
- **SDK client vs. provider endpoint mismatch** (2026-08-05, Wk1 app.py): set `openai.api_key` to a Groq key, but never overrode `base_url` — SDK still points at OpenAI's servers by default. Setting a key ≠ pointing at the right server. Watch for repeats when swapping providers behind an OpenAI-compatible SDK (Groq, Together, OpenRouter, etc.).
- **Legacy vs. current API shape** (2026-08-05, Wk1 app.py): called `completions.create(prompt=...)` (legacy text-completion endpoint) against a chat model — needed `chat.completions.create(messages=[...])`. Watch for repeats confusing older tutorial code with current chat-based APIs.

| 8 | Multi-tool orchestration, memory/state | Agent w/ 2-3 tools, multi-step task |
| 9 | Evals for non-deterministic systems, RAGAS/LangSmith | Eval harness + guardrails |
| 10 | Token cost math, latency sources, caching | Instrument cost/latency tracking |
| 11 | Model routing, prompt caching, batching | Implement 1-2 optimizations, measure |
| 12 | — | Polish all 3, public writeups — **Checkpoint 1 major** |

### Checkpoint 1 (major, end of month 3) — pass criteria
- [ ] 3 projects public + deployed (not just repos)
- [ ] Each has an eval or measured before/after
- [ ] Can explain every architectural choice under questioning
- [ ] One honest written failure case per project

Short on 1-2 → spend an extra week here before Phase 2. This gate matters more than the calendar.

## After Phase 1

- **Phase 2** (mo 4-6): DSA (NeetCode150/Blind75) + system design basics + pick specialization (leaning Context Engineering / Agentic AI Engineering; LLMOps backup)
- **Phase 3** (mo 7-12): specialization depth, project #2, visibility, resume v1
- **Phase 4** (mo 13-18): market readiness, mock interviews
- **Phase 5** (mo 19-24+): apply in batches, track outcomes

Full detail for these phases lives in [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md) — only Phase 1/2 are planned week-by-week on purpose.

## Resources (Phase 1)

- Anthropic Messages API docs, OpenAI API docs
- DeepLearning.AI short courses (free) — prompt engineering, RAG, agentic RAG
- Pydantic docs
- LangChain / LangGraph docs
- pgvector / Chroma / Qdrant
- RAGAS, LangSmith
- Render / Railway / Fly.io (deploy)

## Working rules for this repo

- Don't skip checkpoints — they're the anti-rabbit-hole mechanism.
- Every deliverable ships public (repo/demo/writeup), not left private.
- When user drifts off current week's scope, redirect back to it.
- User's global CLAUDE.md still applies (junior-dev teaching mode, explain WHY, flag "💡 Learn this" concepts, tests alongside code, no debug prints, direct communication).

## Architecture diagrams (Excalidraw)

Maintain a living system-design/architecture diagram per project via the Excalidraw MCP server (already configured — `mcp__excalidraw__*` tools). Update it incrementally, don't regenerate from scratch, every time new code or a structural change lands during that week's session.

- One diagram per project: wk1-3 tool, wk4-6 RAG system, wk7-9 agent (3 total across Phase 1)
- Update after each build session, not just at project end — diagram tracks current code, not the final design
- Use `create_element` / `batch_create_elements` for new components, `update_element` for changed ones, `delete_element` for removed ones. Never `clear_canvas` + redraw — that loses history
- Show real system boundaries: scripts/modules, API calls (incl. which provider/endpoint), data stores, external services, request/response flow — not abstract concepts
- When a snapshot is needed for a project writeup, use `export_scene` or `get_canvas_screenshot`

## Recurring small-detail gaps (watch + reinforce)

Track patterns here when Ved hits the same *kind* of bug more than once, so foundations actually solidify instead of getting patched over each time.

- **Env var loading order** (2026-08-05, Wk1 app.py): wrote `os.getenv()` in a file that never called `load_dotenv()` — had it in a separate `config.py` that was never imported. `.env` is inert until something loads it *before* the read happens; import order matters. Watch for repeats when adding new scripts/modules that need secrets.
- **SDK client vs. provider endpoint mismatch** (2026-08-05, Wk1 app.py): set `openai.api_key` to a Groq key, but never overrode `base_url` — SDK still points at OpenAI's servers by default. Setting a key ≠ pointing at the right server. Watch for repeats when swapping providers behind an OpenAI-compatible SDK (Groq, Together, OpenRouter, etc.).
- **Legacy vs. current API shape** (2026-08-05, Wk1 app.py): called `completions.create(prompt=...)` (legacy text-completion endpoint) against a chat model — needed `chat.completions.create(messages=[...])`. Watch for repeats confusing older tutorial code with current chat-based APIs.

# AI Career Roadmap — Project Context

Full plan: [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md). This file is the working-session summary.

## Who's working here

22yo, BTech CSE, ~6mo Junior SWE (AI/ML), Hyderabad, ₹6 LPA. Knows Python, FastAPI (not pro), Docker, some React/Java, RAG/LLM/LangChain basics.

Redoing Phase 1 on purpose — not first exposure. Goal: verify fundamentals, catch gaps, actually ship the 3 projects. Don't over-explain things already known; probe first.

## Current status

**Phase 1 — Foundation (mo 1-3, wk 1-12).** Starting at Week 1.

Update this line as weeks/checkpoints complete: `Currently: Week X — <topic>`.

## Phase 1 target (12 weeks)

3 public, deployed, evaluated projects:
1. LLM tool, structured output + tool calling (wk 1-3)
2. RAG system w/ citations, deployed (wk 4-6)
3. Tool-using agent w/ eval harness (wk 7-9)

Wk 10-12: cost/latency optimization + polish + writeups across all three.

Learning:building ratio ~40:60 this phase — lean toward building.

## Week-by-week (Phase 1)

| Wk | Learn | Build |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | System/user prompts, few-shot, hosted model API | CLI script: prompt → raw text |
| 2 | Forced JSON output, Pydantic validation, retry-on-invalid | Typed/validated JSON output |
| 3 | Tool/function calling schemas | Finish tool, README, public repo |
| 4 | Embeddings, chunking strategies | Chunk a real corpus |
| 5 | Vector DB, similarity + hybrid search | Index corpus, basic retrieval |
| 6 | Context assembly, citations | Full RAG + deploy (Render/Railway/Fly.io) — **Checkpoint 1** |
| 7 | Agent loops, ReAct, LangGraph | Minimal agent, 1 real tool |
| 8 | Multi-tool orchestration, memory/state | Agent w/ 2-3 tools, multi-step task |
| 9 | Evals for non-deterministic systems, RAGAS/LangSmith | Eval harness + guardrails |
| 10 | Token cost math, latency sources, caching | Instrument cost/latency tracking |
| 11 | Model routing, prompt caching, batching | Implement 1-2 optimizations, measure |
| 12 | — | Polish all 3, public writeups — **Checkpoint 1 major** |

### Checkpoint 1 (major, end of month 3) — pass criteria
- [ ] 3 projects public + deployed (not just repos)
- [ ] Each has an eval or measured before/after
- [ ] Can explain every architectural choice under questioning
- [ ] One honest written failure case per project

Short on 1-2 → spend an extra week here before Phase 2. This gate matters more than the calendar.

## After Phase 1

- **Phase 2** (mo 4-6): DSA (NeetCode150/Blind75) + system design basics + pick specialization (leaning Context Engineering / Agentic AI Engineering; LLMOps backup)
- **Phase 3** (mo 7-12): specialization depth, project #2, visibility, resume v1
- **Phase 4** (mo 13-18): market readiness, mock interviews
- **Phase 5** (mo 19-24+): apply in batches, track outcomes

Full detail for these phases lives in [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md) — only Phase 1/2 are planned week-by-week on purpose.

Roadmap lives at `c:\AI_learning\ai_career_roadmap.md`. Full source of truth — read it directly for exact week-by-week detail; this memory is the navigable summary.

**Structure:** 5 phases over ~24mo (~17-18 hrs/wk).

- **Phase 1 — Foundation** (mo 1-3 / wk 1-12): LLM apps, RAG, agents, evals. Ship 3 public deployed projects: (1) structured-output LLM tool w/ tool calling, (2) RAG system w/ citations, (3) tool-using agent w/ eval harness. Week-by-week breakdown exists (wk1 prompting/API → wk2 structured output/Pydantic → wk3 tool calling+ship → wk4 embeddings/chunking → wk5 vector store/retrieval → wk6 full RAG+deploy [Checkpoint 1] → wk7 agent fundamentals → wk8 multi-tool agents → wk9 evals/guardrails → wk10 cost/latency → wk11 optimization → wk12 polish [Checkpoint 1 major]). Learning:building ratio ~40:60.
- **Phase 2 — Consolidation** (mo 4-6 / wk 13-26): DSA patterns (NeetCode150/Blind75) + system design basics + pick specialization (leaning Context Engineering or Agentic AI Engineering, LLMOps as backup). ~50:50.
- **Phase 3 — Specialization** (mo 7-12): deep in chosen lane, 2nd major project, DSA maintenance, visibility (write-ups), advanced system design, resume v1. ~20:80.
- **Phase 4 — Market readiness** (mo 13-18): resume iteration, networking, mock interviews. ~10:90.
- **Phase 5 — Application** (mo 19-24+): apply in batches via referrals, track in spreadsheet, expect 6-14wk loops/company. ~5:95.

**Checkpoints are load-bearing** — major ones at end of mo3, mo6, mo12, mo18 (readiness gate). Each has explicit pass criteria in the doc; don't skip.

**Status as of 2026-08-05:** Restarting Phase 1 week 1 in Claude Code (not browser Claude) for hands-on execution. User already knows Phase 1 basics conceptually — this pass is verification/gap-filling + actually building the 3 projects, not first exposure.

**Why re-plan only wk1-26 in detail:** doc explicitly avoids false precision beyond mo6; phases 3-5 are monthly blocks meant to be re-planned as he arrives.

**How to apply:** Track which week/phase he's actually on as sessions progress (this will drift from the doc's calendar since he may move faster) — update this memory's "Status" line as he completes weeks/checkpoints. When he asks "what's next" or seems adrift, anchor back to current week's Learn/Build/Resources from the source doc rather than improvising new scope.

**Structure:** 5 phases over ~24mo (~17-18 hrs/wk).

- **Phase 1 — Foundation** (mo 1-3 / wk 1-12): LLM apps, RAG, agents, evals. Ship 3 public deployed projects: (1) structured-output LLM tool w/ tool calling, (2) RAG system w/ citations, (3) tool-using agent w/ eval harness. Week-by-week breakdown exists (wk1 prompting/API → wk2 structured output/Pydantic → wk3 tool calling+ship → wk4 embeddings/chunking → wk5 vector store/retrieval → wk6 full RAG+deploy [Checkpoint 1] → wk7 agent fundamentals → wk8 multi-tool agents → wk9 evals/guardrails → wk10 cost/latency → wk11 optimization → wk12 polish [Checkpoint 1 major]). Learning:building ratio ~40:60.

Roadmap lives at `c:\AI_learning\ai_career_roadmap.md`. Full source of truth — read it directly for exact week-by-week detail; this memory is the navigable summary.

**Structure:** 5 phases over ~24mo (~17-18 hrs/wk).

- **Phase 1 — Foundation** (mo 1-3 / wk 1-12): LLM apps, RAG, agents, evals. Ship 3 public deployed projects: (1) structured-output LLM tool w/ tool calling, (2) RAG system w/ citations, (3) tool-using agent w/ eval harness. Week-by-week breakdown exists (wk1 prompting/API → wk2 structured output/Pydantic → wk3 tool calling+ship → wk4 embeddings/chunking → wk5 vector store/retrieval → wk6 full RAG+deploy [Checkpoint 1] → wk7 agent fundamentals → wk8 multi-tool agents → wk9 evals/guardrails → wk10 cost/latency → wk11 optimization → wk12 polish [Checkpoint 1 major]). Learning:building ratio ~40:60.
- **Phase 2 — Consolidation** (mo 4-6 / wk 13-26): DSA patterns (NeetCode150/Blind75) + system design basics + pick specialization (leaning Context Engineering or Agentic AI Engineering, LLMOps as backup). ~50:50.
- **Phase 3 — Specialization** (mo 7-12): deep in chosen lane, 2nd major project, DSA maintenance, visibility (write-ups), advanced system design, resume v1. ~20:80.
- **Phase 4 — Market readiness** (mo 13-18): resume iteration, networking, mock interviews. ~10:90.
- **Phase 5 — Application** (mo 19-24+): apply in batches via referrals, track in spreadsheet, expect 6-14wk loops/company. ~5:95.

Question for you: have you used `tools=[...]` param before (LangChain agent internals count), or is this first time seeing raw API-level tool calling (no framework)? Answer shapes how much I probe vs skip.

Good — from-scratch is the right rep for this stage. Dropping caveman for this part; multi-step spec needs to read clean, not fragmented.

## Week 3 build spec (write this yourself, I'll review after)

**Folder:** `week03-tool-calling/` — same pattern as week01/02 (`app.py`, `config.py`, `.env`, `requirements.txt`, tests, venv).

**Pick a tool.** Something with a real external effect beats a fake calculator — e.g. a `get_weather(city)` (call a real free weather API) or `search_wikipedia(query)`. Two tools is better than one — forces the model to actually choose, not just always call the only option.

**The round trip** (this is the core mechanic, not obvious from theory alone):

1. Define each tool as a JSON schema: `name`, `description`, `parameters` (JSON Schema: `type: object`, `properties`, `required`). Description quality matters — it's the only thing the model uses to decide when to call it.
2. First API call: send `messages` + `tools=[...]`. Groq is OpenAI-compatible here, but **confirm exact param shape in Groq's docs before coding** — don't assume it matches something you remember from a tutorial (Week 1's `completions` vs `chat.completions` bug was exactly this kind of unchecked assumption).
3. Check `response.choices[0].message.tool_calls`. If present, model wants tool(s) called, not a text answer.
4. `tool_calls[i].function.arguments` is a **JSON string**, not a dict — needs `json.loads()`. 💡 Learn this: forgetting this parse step is a natural spot to reproduce Week 2's silent-wrong-data bug pattern (except here it throws instead of silently passing).
5. Dispatch to your real Python function by `function.name` (dict lookup: `{"get_weather": get_weather, ...}`, not if/elif chains).
6. Append the assistant's tool-call message AND a new `role: "tool"` message (with matching `tool_call_id` and the function's result as `content`) back into `messages`.
7. Call the model again with the extended `messages`. Now it answers in natural language using the tool result.

**Multi-step:** wrap 3-7 in a loop — some prompts need 2+ tool calls before the model is ready to answer in text. Loop until `tool_calls` is empty.

**Tests:** mock the client same as Week 2. Verify: correct tool gets picked for a given prompt, arguments parse correctly, dispatch calls the right function, loop terminates.

**README + public repo** — due this week per roadmap. Don't defer to "later."

Ping me with your first draft or wherever you get stuck.

# AI-first career roadmap: junior engineer → high-paying product / FAANG-tier role

**Starting point:** 22, BTech CSE, ~6 months into a Junior SWE (AI/ML) role in Hyderabad, ₹6 LPA. Know Python, FastAPI (not at pro level), Docker, a little React and Java, and the basics of RAG/LLMs/LangChain.

**Weekly time budget used in this plan:** ~17-18 hrs/week (2 hrs on weekdays, 3-4 hrs on weekends).

**Horizon:** ~24 months, in 5 phases. Weeks 1-26 (months 1-6) are planned week by week, because that's the part worth planning precisely. Beyond month 6, the plan moves to monthly blocks on purpose — pretending to know exactly what week 43 looks like today would be false precision. You'll re-plan the far phases as you get there, using the checkpoints in this doc.

---

## How to read this document

- **Learning : building ratio** changes by phase — heavy on learning early, heavy on building later. It's called out per phase.
- **Self-eval checkpoints** are placed at natural phase boundaries. Don't skip them — they're the mechanism that stops "preparing" from becoming an identity instead of a phase.
- **Resources** are consolidated in one master list near the end so you're not hunting through the whole doc.
- Every project deliverable should end up **public** (a repo, a deployed demo, a short writeup) — private, unfinished work doesn't compound the way shipped work does.

---

## Phase overview

| Phase | Duration | Focus | Learning : building |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Foundation | Months 1-3 (wk 1-12) | LLM apps, RAG, agents, evals — 3 shipped projects | ~40:60 |
| 2. Consolidation | Months 4-6 (wk 13-26) | DSA patterns + system design basics + pick a specialization | ~50:50 |
| 3. Specialization | Months 7-12 | Go deep in one AI-engineering lane, second major project | ~20:80 |
| 4. Market readiness | Months 13-18 | Resume, networking, mock interviews, visibility | ~10:90 |
| 5. Application | Months 19-24+ | Apply, interview, negotiate | ~5:95 |

---

## Phase 1 — Foundation (months 1-3, weeks 1-12)

Goal by end of phase: **3 public, deployed, evaluated projects** — an LLM tool with structured output, a RAG system, and a tool-using agent with an eval harness.

### Week 1 — Prompting and API basics
- **Learn:** system/user prompts, few-shot prompting, calling a hosted model API from Python.
- **Build:** a CLI script that sends a prompt and returns raw text.
- **Resources:** Anthropic's Messages API docs, OpenAI API docs, DeepLearning.AI's short course on prompt engineering for developers (free).
- Split this week: ~60% learning / 40% building — new territory.

### Week 2 — Structured output and validation
- **Learn:** forcing a model to return JSON, validating it with Pydantic, retry-on-invalid-output patterns.
- **Build:** extend last week's tool to return typed, validated JSON instead of raw text.
- **Resources:** Pydantic docs, Anthropic/OpenAI structured-output docs.

### Week 3 — Tool/function calling, ship it
- **Learn:** function/tool-calling schemas, basic multi-tool patterns.
- **Build:** finish the tool — add tool calling, clean it up, write a README, push to a public GitHub repo.
- **Checkpoint (mini):** can you explain every design decision in this tool if someone questions it? If not, that's this week's real task, not more building.

### Week 4 — Embeddings and chunking
- **Learn:** what embeddings are, chunking strategies (fixed-size, recursive, semantic).
- **Build:** pick a real corpus you care about (your own notes, a public dataset, docs from a product you use) and chunk it.
- **Resources:** a free vector-database/RAG short course (DeepLearning.AI or Google Cloud's free options), pgvector docs.

### Week 5 — Vector store and retrieval
- **Learn:** vector DB basics, similarity search, hybrid search (keyword + dense).
- **Build:** index your chunked corpus, get basic retrieval working end to end.
- **Resources:** pgvector (fits your Postgres/backend world directly) or Chroma/Qdrant for faster prototyping.

### Week 6 — Full RAG, citations, deploy
- **Learn:** assembling retrieved context into a prompt, citing sources in the answer.
- **Build:** complete the RAG system with citations, deploy a demo (Render/Railway/Fly.io free tiers all work), publish it.
- **Checkpoint 1 (end of month 1.5):** does retrieval actually improve answers on your corpus? Find and write down 2-3 cases where it fails. Being able to say *why* it fails is more valuable than pretending it's perfect.

### Week 7 — Agent fundamentals
- **Learn:** agent loops (plan → act → observe), the ReAct pattern, LangGraph or a hand-rolled loop.
- **Build:** a minimal agent with one real tool (e.g., a calculator, a web search call, a database query).
- **Resources:** LangGraph docs, Anthropic's docs on building agents.

### Week 8 — Multi-tool agents and memory
- **Learn:** orchestrating multiple tools, designing short-term memory/state.
- **Build:** extend your agent to 2-3 real tools completing a small multi-step task.

### Week 9 — Evals and guardrails
- **Learn:** what makes evaluating a non-deterministic system different from a unit test; RAGAS/LangSmith concepts.
- **Build:** an eval harness that scores your agent against a fixed set of tasks, plus basic guardrails against bad actions.
- **Resources:** RAGAS docs, LangSmith docs.
- **Checkpoint (mini):** run the eval before and after one deliberate change to the agent. Can you point to a number that moved?

### Week 10 — Cost and latency profiling
- **Learn:** token cost math, where latency actually comes from, caching strategies.
- **Build:** instrument your RAG/agent projects with cost and latency tracking.

### Week 11 — Optimization
- **Learn:** model routing (cheap model for easy cases, expensive for hard ones), prompt caching, batching.
- **Build:** implement 1-2 optimizations on an existing project, measure before/after.

### Week 12 — Polish, document, self-eval
- **Build:** clean up all three projects, write a short public post for each explaining what you tried, what failed, and what the numbers showed.
- **✅ Checkpoint 1 — major (end of month 3):**
  - [ ] 3 projects, all public, all deployed (not just repos)
  - [ ] Each has an eval or a measured before/after
  - [ ] You can explain every architectural choice under questioning
  - [ ] You've written up at least one honest failure case per project

If you're short on 1-2 of these, spend an extra week here before moving on. This checkpoint matters more than staying on schedule.

---

## Phase 2 — Consolidation (months 4-6, weeks 13-26)

Goal: build the DSA + system-design spine that FAANG-tier interviews still test regardless of role, and pick your AI specialization based on real signal from Phase 1 (which project did you enjoy most?).

| Weeks | DSA focus | Other focus |
|---|---|---|
| 13-14 | Arrays, hashing, two pointers | — |
| 15-16 | Sliding window, stacks/queues | Intro to system design (scalability basics) |
| 17-18 | Trees, BFS/DFS | **Pick your specialization** (see below) |
| 19-20 | Graphs, backtracking | Start specialization project #2 |
| 21-22 | DP fundamentals | Continue specialization project #2 |
| 23-24 | Mixed review | System design deep dive: caching, sharding, queues, consistency |
| 25-26 | Buffer / catch-up | Finish specialization project #2 |

**Picking a specialization:** based on the futurense/2026 market breakdown, your natural first choice is **Context Engineering** (RAG, retrieval, memory design) or **Agentic AI Engineering** (tool-using agents) — both build directly on Phase 1 and your existing LangChain exposure. **LLMOps/AI Infrastructure** is a strong second option given your Docker background. Don't overthink this — you can pivot later; the point is to go deep in *something* rather than staying shallow in everything.

**Resources for this phase:** NeetCode 150 or Blind 75 (work pattern by pattern, not randomly), "Designing Data-Intensive Applications" by Martin Kleppmann (the standard system-design reference, still evergreen), a pattern-based system design course if you want structure (look for a current, well-reviewed one — these get updated often).

**✅ Checkpoint 2 — major (end of month 6):**
- [ ] 120-150 DSA problems solved with real pattern recognition (not memorized)
- [ ] Can explain time/space complexity of your own solutions without prompting
- [ ] Comfortable sketching basic system-design concepts (caching, load balancing, a simple RAG-at-scale design)
- [ ] Specialization chosen, project #2 underway or done
- [ ] ~2 years total runway used so far: 6 months down, on pace

---

## Phase 3 — Specialization (months 7-12)

This is monthly, not weekly — the work gets less script-able and more like real engineering judgment from here.

- **Month 7:** Go deep in your chosen lane. Context/Agentic → graph RAG, multimodal retrieval, MCP integration. LLMOps → prompt versioning tooling, monitoring/observability stacks.
- **Month 8:** Second major specialization project — aim for something with real usage, not just a demo. If your company will let you own a small AI feature at work, that's worth more than any side project.
- **Month 9:** DSA maintenance (3-4 hrs/week is enough now, don't let it fully lapse), first light mock-interview practice.
- **Month 10:** Build visibility — 2-3 technical write-ups, tidy GitHub/LinkedIn into something that tells a coherent story of what you build.
- **Month 11:** Advanced system design (real case studies: design a rate limiter, design a RAG system at scale, design a notification system).
- **Month 12:** Draft resume v1, run your first real mock interview.

**✅ Checkpoint 3 — major (end of month 12):**
- [ ] 2 specialization projects with real depth, one with real/production usage if at all possible
- [ ] DSA still sharp (medium problems in 25-30 min)
- [ ] Resume draft exists and has been reviewed by at least one other engineer
- [ ] You've done one full mock interview and gotten specific feedback
- [ ] Gap analysis: what's the weakest of the four (DSA / system design / AI depth / communication)? That's month 13's priority.

---

## Phase 4 — Market readiness (months 13-18)

- **Months 13-14:** Iterate the resume against real job descriptions. Start networking deliberately on LinkedIn — comment, post about your projects, connect with engineers at target companies.
- **Months 15-16:** Regular mock interviews (DSA + system design + behavioral). Consider one opportunistic off-campus application as a real-world data point, even if it feels early.
- **Months 17-18:** Final polish pass on projects and resume.

**✅ Checkpoint 4 — the big readiness gate (end of month 18):** Go through the full readiness checklist below. This is the one that decides whether phase 5 starts on schedule or gets another 2-3 months.

---

## Phase 5 — Application and interview (months 19-24+)

- Apply in batches, referrals first. Track every application, interview stage, and outcome in a spreadsheet — you need this to spot patterns (weak resume screen vs weak interview performance are different problems with different fixes).
- Expect a 6-14 week loop per company, and a typical 6-12 month cool-off after a rejection before reapplying — plan your target list accordingly instead of burning all your shots at once.
- Know the quirks going in: Amazon's loop is leadership-principle-heavy (prep behavioral stories properly), Google runs team-matching after the hiring committee stage. Every company has similar idiosyncrasies — look them up before the loop, not during.
- Cast a genuinely wide net across the tier you're targeting: Google/Meta/Amazon alongside Microsoft, Adobe, Salesforce, Walmart Global Tech, Uber, and top Indian product companies. Don't over-index on 3-4 dream names.

---

## The readiness checklist (use this instead of a feeling)

"Am I ready" is not a feeling to wait for — it's this list. You don't need 100% to start applying; ~70% is enough, because real interviews are themselves part of the training loop.

**Technical**
- [ ] Solve a fresh LeetCode medium in under 25-30 minutes without help
- [ ] Explain time/space complexity of your own code unprompted
- [ ] Whiteboard a basic system design (URL shortener, RAG-at-scale, rate limiter) in 30-45 minutes
- [ ] 2-3 deployed, evaluated AI projects you can defend in detail
- [ ] Comfortable saying "here's where this breaks and why," not just "it works"

**Process**
- [ ] Resume gets shortlisted at a reasonable rate (rough benchmark: 15-20%+ callback on well-targeted applications — if you're well below this, the resume is the bug, not your skills)
- [ ] Survived at least 2-3 real mock interviews without major stumbles
- [ ] Have a specific, named target list, not just "FAANG"

**When to actually start applying (vs. keep prepping forever):**
1. You've hit roughly 70% of the checklist above.
2. You've got enough tenure at your current job that switching doesn't read as job-hopping — in the Indian market, 18-24 months at your first job is generally a safe minimum before your first move.
3. Your current role has stopped teaching you anything new month-over-month — that's a much better trigger than a calendar date.
4. You notice you're adding "just one more" project or course before applying — that's usually avoidance, not genuine unreadiness. Apply anyway; you'll learn more from three real interviews than from another month of solo prep.

---

## Master resource list

**DSA**
- NeetCode 150 / Blind 75 — pattern-based practice, not random problems
- LeetCode — for volume once patterns are solid

**System design**
- *Designing Data-Intensive Applications* (Kleppmann) — the standard reference, still evergreen
- A current pattern-based system design course (check reviews — this category updates often)

**AI / LLM engineering**
- DeepLearning.AI short courses (free) — prompting, RAG, agentic RAG
- LangChain / LangGraph official docs
- Anthropic's docs on tool use, building agents, and MCP (Model Context Protocol)
- Pydantic docs (structured output validation)

**Vector stores & evals**
- pgvector (fits a Postgres/backend stack directly), Chroma, Qdrant
- RAGAS and LangSmith for evaluation frameworks

**Deployment**
- Render, Railway, or Fly.io free tiers for demo hosting
- GitHub Actions basics for a simple CI pipeline on your projects

---

## The one-paragraph version

Ship three real AI projects in the first 90 days using what you already know from backend work. Spend months 4-6 building the DSA and system-design spine that FAANG-tier interviews still require. Go deep in one AI specialization for the next six months while keeping the fundamentals warm. Spend six months making that work visible and interview-ready. Then apply — in batches, through referrals where possible, tracking everything — and treat early rejections as data, not verdicts. Total runway: about 18-24 months of consistent, unspectacular effort at roughly 17 hours a week. That's the whole plan.

aiTitle: Review AI career roadmap and learning plan

input.content:
---
name: user-ai-career-profile
description: Ved's background, current role, and career-switch goal into AI engineering
metadata:
  type: user
---

22yo, BTech CSE. ~6mo into Junior SWE (AI/ML) role, Hyderabad, ₹6 LPA. Employer: Stackular (per email domain).

Known stack: Python, FastAPI (not pro level yet), Docker, little React, little Java, basics of RAG/LLMs/LangChain.

Goal: FAANG-tier / high-paying AI engineering role within ~24mo. Built [[project-ai-career-roadmap]] via Claude (browser) to structure this — now redoing Phase 1 in Claude Code even though basics known, to re-verify fundamentals and catch gaps, not because he's starting cold.

Time budget: ~17-18 hrs/wk (2hrs weekdays, 3-4hrs weekends). Pace is a floor not a ceiling — he expects to move faster than the week-by-week plan in places.

input.content:
# AI Career Roadmap — Project Context

Full plan: [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md). This file is the working-session summary.

## Who's working here

22yo, BTech CSE, ~6mo Junior SWE (AI/ML), Hyderabad, ₹6 LPA. Knows Python, FastAPI (not pro), Docker, some React/Java, RAG/LLM/LangChain basics.

Redoing Phase 1 on purpose — not first exposure. Goal: verify fundamentals, catch gaps, actually ship the 3 projects. Don't over-explain things already known; probe first.

## Current status

**Phase 1 — Foundation (mo 1-3, wk 1-12).** Starting at Week 1.

Update this line as weeks/checkpoints complete: `Currently: Week X — <topic>`.

## Phase 1 target (12 weeks)

3 public, deployed, evaluated projects:
1. LLM tool, structured output + tool calling (wk 1-3)
2. RAG system w/ citations, deployed (wk 4-6)
3. Tool-using agent w/ eval harness (wk 7-9)

Wk 10-12: cost/latency optimization + polish + writeups across all three.

Learning:building ratio ~40:60 this phase — lean toward building.

## Week-by-week (Phase 1)

| Wk | Learn | Build |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | System/user prompts, few-shot, hosted model API | CLI script: prompt → raw text |
| 2 | Forced JSON output, Pydantic validation, retry-on-invalid | Typed/validated JSON output |
| 3 | Tool/function calling schemas | Finish tool, README, public repo |
| 4 | Embeddings, chunking strategies | Chunk a real corpus |
| 5 | Vector DB, similarity + hybrid search | Index corpus, basic retrieval |
| 6 | Context assembly, citations | Full RAG + deploy (Render/Railway/Fly.io) — **Checkpoint 1** |
| 7 | Agent loops, ReAct, LangGraph | Minimal agent, 1 real tool |
| 8 | Multi-tool orchestration, memory/state | Agent w/ 2-3 tools, multi-step task |
| 9 | Evals for non-deterministic systems, RAGAS/LangSmith | Eval harness + guardrails |
| 10 | Token cost math, latency sources, caching | Instrument cost/latency tracking |
| 11 | Model routing, prompt caching, batching | Implement 1-2 optimizations, measure |
| 12 | — | Polish all 3, public writeups — **Checkpoint 1 major** |

### Checkpoint 1 (major, end of month 3) — pass criteria
- [ ] 3 projects public + deployed (not just repos)
- [ ] Each has an eval or measured before/after
- [ ] Can explain every architectural choice under questioning
- [ ] One honest written failure case per project

Short on 1-2 → spend an extra week here before Phase 2. This gate matters more than the calendar.

## After Phase 1

- **Phase 2** (mo 4-6): DSA (NeetCode150/Blind75) + system design basics + pick specialization (leaning Context Engineering / Agentic AI Engineering; LLMOps backup)
- **Phase 3** (mo 7-12): specialization depth, project #2, visibility, resume v1
- **Phase 4** (mo 13-18): market readiness, mock interviews
- **Phase 5** (mo 19-24+): apply in batches, track outcomes

Full detail for these phases lives in [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md) — only Phase 1/2 are planned week-by-week on purpose.

## Resources (Phase 1)

- Anthropic Messages API docs, OpenAI API docs
- DeepLearning.AI short courses (free) — prompt engineering, RAG, agentic RAG
- Pydantic docs
- LangChain / LangGraph docs
- pgvector / Chroma / Qdrant
- RAGAS, LangSmith
- Render / Railway / Fly.io (deploy)

## Working rules for this repo

- Don't skip checkpoints — they're the anti-rabbit-hole mechanism.
- Every deliverable ships public (repo/demo/writeup), not left private.
- When user drifts off current week's scope, redirect back to it.
- User's global CLAUDE.md still applies (junior-dev teaching mode, explain WHY, flag "💡 Learn this" concepts, tests alongside code, no debug prints, direct communication).

| 10 | Token cost math, latency sources, caching | Instrument cost/latency tracking |
| 11 | Model routing, prompt caching, batching | Implement 1-2 optimizations, measure |
| 12 | — | Polish all 3, public writeups — **Checkpoint 1 major** |

### Checkpoint 1 (major, end of month 3) — pass criteria
- [ ] 3 projects public + deployed (not just repos)
- [ ] Each has an eval or measured before/after
- [ ] Can explain every architectural choice under questioning
- [ ] One honest written failure case per project

Short on 1-2 → spend an extra week here before Phase 2. This gate matters more than the calendar.

## After Phase 1

- **Phase 2** (mo 4-6): DSA (NeetCode150/Blind75) + system design basics + pick specialization (leaning Context Engineering / Agentic AI Engineering; LLMOps backup)
- **Phase 3** (mo 7-12): specialization depth, project #2, visibility, resume v1
- **Phase 4** (mo 13-18): market readiness, mock interviews
- **Phase 5** (mo 19-24+): apply in batches, track outcomes

Full detail for these phases lives in [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md) — only Phase 1/2 are planned week-by-week on purpose.

## Resources (Phase 1)

- Anthropic Messages API docs, OpenAI API docs
- DeepLearning.AI short courses (free) — prompt engineering, RAG, agentic RAG
- Pydantic docs
- LangChain / LangGraph docs
- pgvector / Chroma / Qdrant
- RAGAS, LangSmith
- Render / Railway / Fly.io (deploy)

## Working rules for this repo

- Don't skip checkpoints — they're the anti-rabbit-hole mechanism.
- Every deliverable ships public (repo/demo/writeup), not left private.
- When user drifts off current week's scope, redirect back to it.
- User's global CLAUDE.md still applies (junior-dev teaching mode, explain WHY, flag "💡 Learn this" concepts, tests alongside code, no debug prints, direct communication).

content.text:
1. System prompt vs user prompt — diff, when each?
- System prompt is the prompt that is given to the model along with the user prompt or before the user prompt is sent. The system prompt contains information about how the model should behave, how the model should talk to the user, how it should respond, the tone, the language, the answer format, the role it should take, basically all the ways you want the model to behave. Whereas the user prompt is the prompt that is sent by the user, which basically infers to what the user wants. It is the user question, any task it wants the model to do etc. System prompt is the how, user prompt is the what for the model.

2. Few-shot prompting — what is it, why help model?
- This is a concept of giving the model some similar question with the answer examples from the user side, for the model to align well with the pattern for it to understand that the incoming questions or tasks that the user wants it do to follows the above pattern. This works really well and increases the model output. The reason we help the model is because, at the end of the day, a model is just an LLM, which is a nueral network architecture, that means it makes connections based on patters, and the better input pattern you give the better output patterns it will work on and give the output in a much better way.

3. Forcing JSON output from LLM — how? (name a method/technique)
- As much as i know, we can force a JSON output from an LLM by using Pydantic models, these models have a fixed state of inputs and outputs defined with their data types and default values which is given to the model and the output is always given in that format and validated by pydantic to make sure it is correct. This is mostly done to keep a fixed output type to easily handle the LLM output data, and also not cause hallucinations and to catch hallucinations of the LLMs. I dont know if there is a method or technique called for it.

4. Why validate LLM JSON output w/ Pydantic instead of trusting it raw?
- Because LLMs can hallucinate. Also, the output format of each LLM witout having pydantic makes it harder to take out all the data from the output, manully, and having to check or trust the LLM that it is generating actual data types specific outputs that we want is risky, hence using pydantic saves time and forces the LLM to output in a certain way which makes it easy for us to handle the output data as well. 

5. Retry-on-invalid-output — what pattern would you use if model returns bad JSON?
- As much as i know, i will put a loop for the LLM to try n amount of times, if after n turns it still gives bad output, then i dont validate it, just ask it to return the output, and will either manually verify it or do some other method. Thats all i know about this.

6. Tool/function calling — explain in your own words how it works (model side vs your code side)
- Tools are basically python functions written with whatever their functionality is, for eg: a calculator tool is a fuctnion in that takes the input as numbers. when a user inputs a model to calculate something, the model first checks the list of tools it has, if it finds a tool that can do the work that is asked, it calls that python function with the input the users gave, waits for that python fn to return the answer and takes that python fn result and when the LLM gets it, the result is given to the user. this prevents the LLM doing the calculator operation which can most of the times be wrong. Model side the tool calling is done via the LLM, and the code side the tool is basically a function written with a @tool decorator, which makes the LLM  know that this is a tool that cna be used. Fucntion calling i presume are just normal functions that can be called by the model. they are standar python functions.

7. If given 3 tools, how does model decide which to call, and how does result get back to it?
- The user intput and the tool call description decices which tool gets called. If the input asks the model to get live score of a football match, the model searches for tools, and reads each tools description to see if it matches to what the user is aksing, if it does, for instance here the web search tool, the model send the input as per that tool call, which then searches it on the internet via the API, and gets the result, gives it back to the LLM which then formats it into an answer and gives it back to the user.

**Diagnostic result: strong. 5/7 solid, 2 real gaps.**

✅ Q1 system/user prompt — correct.
✅ Q2 few-shot — correct, right reasoning (pattern completion via next-token prediction).
✅ Q4 why Pydantic — correct.
✅ Q7 tool selection/round-trip — correct.

⚠️ Q3 — gap. Pydantic isn't what *forces* JSON out the model. Pydantic defines the schema/shape you want. Forcing happens at API level:
- Anthropic: pass tool schema, force `tool_choice` → model's response *is* structured JSON matching that schema (this is how libs like `instructor` fake "structured output" on Anthropic).
- OpenAI: native `response_format={"type":"json_schema",...}` — constrained decoding, model literally can't emit invalid tokens.
Pydantic's job = define schema + validate/parse after. Enforcement mechanism = separate.
💡 Learn this: structured output = (schema definition) + (API-level enforcement). Two different things, you merged them.

⚠️ Q5 — gap, partial. Retry loop right instinct, but real pattern: feed the **validation error back to the model** in the retry ("your last output failed because X, fix it"), not blind retry. And "if n tries fail, skip validation, trust raw" defeats the whole point — real fallback is usually: raise/log failure, surface to caller, never silently accept unvalidated data downstream.
💡 Learn this: retry = correction loop (show model its own error), not just "try again blind."

⚠️ Q6 — mostly right, one imprecision: **model never calls your Python function.** Model returns "I want to call tool X with args Y" (a tool_use block) — a request, not an execution. Your code sees that, executes the actual function, sends the result back as a new message (tool_result), model reads it, continues. `@tool` decorator (LangChain) is a convenience wrapper generating the schema — not the underlying mechanism, that's just JSON schema + multi-turn message passing.

**Verdict:** concepts solid, mental models slightly fuzzy on mechanism (what does the enforcing, who executes what). Good news — this means wk1-2 doesn't need full slow rebuild. 

Proposed: skip separate wk1/wk2 practice, go straight to Week 1 build (CLI script, raw text) today, fold in wk2's structured-output fix immediately after using correct approach (native API structured output, not just Pydantic-and-hope), move faster through wk1-3 since foundation's there. Sound right, or want wk1 build strictly first before touching structured output?

# AI Career Roadmap — Project Context

Full plan: [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md). This file is the working-session summary.

## Who's working here

22yo, BTech CSE, ~6mo Junior SWE (AI/ML), Hyderabad, ₹6 LPA. Knows Python, FastAPI (not pro), Docker, some React/Java, RAG/LLM/LangChain basics.

Redoing Phase 1 on purpose — not first exposure. Goal: verify fundamentals, catch gaps, actually ship the 3 projects. Don't over-explain things already known; probe first.

## Current status

**Phase 1 — Foundation (mo 1-3, wk 1-12).** Starting at Week 1.

Update this line as weeks/checkpoints complete: `Currently: Week X — <topic>`.

## Phase 1 target (12 weeks)

3 public, deployed, evaluated projects:
1. LLM tool, structured output + tool calling (wk 1-3)
2. RAG system w/ citations, deployed (wk 4-6)
3. Tool-using agent w/ eval harness (wk 7-9)

Wk 10-12: cost/latency optimization + polish + writeups across all three.

Learning:building ratio ~40:60 this phase — lean toward building.

## Week-by-week (Phase 1)

| Wk | Learn | Build |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | System/user prompts, few-shot, hosted model API | CLI script: prompt → raw text |
| 2 | Forced JSON output, Pydantic validation, retry-on-invalid | Typed/validated JSON output |
| 3 | Tool/function calling schemas | Finish tool, README, public repo |
| 4 | Embeddings, chunking strategies | Chunk a real corpus |
| 5 | Vector DB, similarity + hybrid search | Index corpus, basic retrieval |
| 6 | Context assembly, citations | Full RAG + deploy (Render/Railway/Fly.io) — **Checkpoint 1** |
| 7 | Agent loops, ReAct, LangGraph | Minimal agent, 1 real tool |
| 8 | Multi-tool orchestration, memory/state | Agent w/ 2-3 tools, multi-step task |
| 9 | Evals for non-deterministic systems, RAGAS/LangSmith | Eval harness + guardrails |
| 10 | Token cost math, latency sources, caching | Instrument cost/latency tracking |
| 11 | Model routing, prompt caching, batching | Implement 1-2 optimizations, measure |
| 12 | — | Polish all 3, public writeups — **Checkpoint 1 major** |

### Checkpoint 1 (major, end of month 3) — pass criteria
- [ ] 3 projects public + deployed (not just repos)
- [ ] Each has an eval or measured before/after
- [ ] Can explain every architectural choice under questioning
- [ ] One honest written failure case per project

Short on 1-2 → spend an extra week here before Phase 2. This gate matters more than the calendar.

## After Phase 1

- **Phase 2** (mo 4-6): DSA (NeetCode150/Blind75) + system design basics + pick specialization (leaning Context Engineering / Agentic AI Engineering; LLMOps backup)
- **Phase 3** (mo 7-12): specialization depth, project #2, visibility, resume v1
- **Phase 4** (mo 13-18): market readiness, mock interviews
- **Phase 5** (mo 19-24+): apply in batches, track outcomes

Full detail for these phases lives in [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md) — only Phase 1/2 are planned week-by-week on purpose.

## Resources (Phase 1)

- Anthropic Messages API docs, OpenAI API docs
- DeepLearning.AI short courses (free) — prompt engineering, RAG, agentic RAG
- Pydantic docs
- LangChain / LangGraph docs
- pgvector / Chroma / Qdrant
- RAGAS, LangSmith
- Render / Railway / Fly.io (deploy)

## Working rules for this repo

- Don't skip checkpoints — they're the anti-rabbit-hole mechanism.
- Every deliverable ships public (repo/demo/writeup), not left private.
- When user drifts off current week's scope, redirect back to it.
- User's global CLAUDE.md still applies (junior-dev teaching mode, explain WHY, flag "💡 Learn this" concepts, tests alongside code, no debug prints, direct communication).

## Recurring small-detail gaps (watch + reinforce)

Track patterns here when Ved hits the same *kind* of bug more than once, so foundations actually solidify instead of getting patched over each time.

- **Env var loading order** (2026-08-05, Wk1 app.py): wrote `os.getenv()` in a file that never called `load_dotenv()` — had it in a separate `config.py` that was never imported. `.env` is inert until something loads it *before* the read happens; import order matters. Watch for repeats when adding new scripts/modules that need secrets.
- **SDK client vs. provider endpoint mismatch** (2026-08-05, Wk1 app.py): set `openai.api_key` to a Groq key, but never overrode `base_url` — SDK still points at OpenAI's servers by default. Setting a key ≠ pointing at the right server. Watch for repeats when swapping providers behind an OpenAI-compatible SDK (Groq, Together, OpenRouter, etc.).
- **Legacy vs. current API shape** (2026-08-05, Wk1 app.py): called `completions.create(prompt=...)` (legacy text-completion endpoint) against a chat model — needed `chat.completions.create(messages=[...])`. Watch for repeats confusing older tutorial code with current chat-based APIs.

Full plan: [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md). This file is the working-session summary.

## Who's working here

22yo, BTech CSE, ~6mo Junior SWE (AI/ML), Hyderabad, ₹6 LPA. Knows Python, FastAPI (not pro), Docker, some React/Java, RAG/LLM/LangChain basics.

Redoing Phase 1 on purpose — not first exposure. Goal: verify fundamentals, catch gaps, actually ship the 3 projects. Don't over-explain things already known; probe first.

## Current status

**Phase 1 — Foundation (mo 1-3, wk 1-12).** Starting at Week 1.

Update this line as weeks/checkpoints complete: `Currently: Week X — <topic>`.

## Phase 1 target (12 weeks)

3 public, deployed, evaluated projects:
1. LLM tool, structured output + tool calling (wk 1-3)
2. RAG system w/ citations, deployed (wk 4-6)
3. Tool-using agent w/ eval harness (wk 7-9)

Wk 10-12: cost/latency optimization + polish + writeups across all three.

Learning:building ratio ~40:60 this phase — lean toward building.

## Week-by-week (Phase 1)

| Wk | Learn | Build |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | System/user prompts, few-shot, hosted model API | CLI script: prompt → raw text |
| 2 | Forced JSON output, Pydantic validation, retry-on-invalid | Typed/validated JSON output |
| 3 | Tool/function calling schemas | Finish tool, README, public repo |
| 4 | Embeddings, chunking strategies | Chunk a real corpus |
| 5 | Vector DB, similarity + hybrid search | Index corpus, basic retrieval |
| 6 | Context assembly, citations | Full RAG + deploy (Render/Railway/Fly.io) — **Checkpoint 1** |
| 7 | Agent loops, ReAct, LangGraph | Minimal agent, 1 real tool |
| 8 | Multi-tool orchestration, memory/state | Agent w/ 2-3 tools, multi-step task |
| 9 | Evals for non-deterministic systems, RAGAS/LangSmith | Eval harness + guardrails |
| 10 | Token cost math, latency sources, caching | Instrument cost/latency tracking |
| 11 | Model routing, prompt caching, batching | Implement 1-2 optimizations, measure |
| 12 | — | Polish all 3, public writeups — **Checkpoint 1 major** |

### Checkpoint 1 (major, end of month 3) — pass criteria
- [ ] 3 projects public + deployed (not just repos)
- [ ] Each has an eval or measured before/after
- [ ] Can explain every architectural choice under questioning
- [ ] One honest written failure case per project

Short on 1-2 → spend an extra week here before Phase 2. This gate matters more than the calendar.

## After Phase 1

- **Phase 2** (mo 4-6): DSA (NeetCode150/Blind75) + system design basics + pick specialization (leaning Context Engineering / Agentic AI Engineering; LLMOps backup)
- **Phase 3** (mo 7-12): specialization depth, project #2, visibility, resume v1
- **Phase 4** (mo 13-18): market readiness, mock interviews
- **Phase 5** (mo 19-24+): apply in batches, track outcomes

Full detail for these phases lives in [ai_career_roadmap.md](ai_career_roadmap.md) — only Phase 1/2 are planned week-by-week on purpose.

## Resources (Phase 1)

- Anthropic Messages API docs, OpenAI API docs
- DeepLearning.AI short courses (free) — prompt engineering, RAG, agentic RAG
- Pydantic docs
- LangChain / LangGraph docs
- pgvector / Chroma / Qdrant
- RAGAS, LangSmith
- Render / Railway / Fly.io (deploy)

## Working rules for this repo

- Don't skip checkpoints — they're the anti-rabbit-hole mechanism.
- Every deliverable ships public (repo/demo/writeup), not left private.
- When user drifts off current week's scope, redirect back to it.
- User's global CLAUDE.md still applies (junior-dev teaching mode, explain WHY, flag "💡 Learn this" concepts, tests alongside code, no debug prints, direct communication).

## Recurring small-detail gaps (watch + reinforce)

Track patterns here when Ved hits the same *kind* of bug more than once, so foundations actually solidify instead of getting patched over each time.

- **Env var loading order** (2026-08-05, Wk1 app.py): wrote `os.getenv()` in a file that never called `load_dotenv()` — had it in a separate `config.py` that was never imported. `.env` is inert until something loads it *before* the read happens; import order matters. Watch for repeats when adding new scripts/modules that need secrets.
- **SDK client vs. provider endpoint mismatch** (2026-08-05, Wk1 app.py): set `openai.api_key` to a Groq key, but never overrode `base_url` — SDK still points at OpenAI's servers by default. Setting a key ≠ pointing at the right server. Watch for repeats when swapping providers behind an OpenAI-compatible SDK (Groq, Together, OpenRouter, etc.).
- **Legacy vs. current API shape** (2026-08-05, Wk1 app.py): called `completions.create(prompt=...)` (legacy text-completion endpoint) against a chat model — needed `chat.completions.create(messages=[...])`. Watch for repeats confusing older tutorial code with current chat-based APIs.
